title: Off-Plan Runs on Believers: How Presale Markets Break, and 5 Warning Signs
seoTitle: Off-Plan Runs on Believers: How Presale Markets Break
description: Toronto went from 31,000 new condo sales to 60 in a quarter. Who the believers are, what happens when they leave, and five signs a storm is coming.
answer: Off-plan real estate runs on belief: towers get built only when enough buyers with money believe a unit will be worth more later. When those believers, often investors, leave, sales collapse even if the money is still there. Toronto shows it: about 31,000 new condo sales in 2021, 1,500 in 2025, and only 60 in three months this summer.
body:
In 2021, buyers in the Toronto region purchased almost 31,000 new condos. Last year the number was about 1,500, a drop of 95%. This summer, over three months, the same region sold 60 pre-construction units. Same city, same skyline, same cranes. So what disappeared? Not the money. The believers.

## Why off-plan runs on belief

New development has one fuel: belief. A tower only gets built when enough people with money believe the unit will be worth more tomorrow than it is today.

Look at how much belief is in the market right now. At the start of 2026, there were about 150 condo projects in pre-construction across downtown Miami, Miami Beach and Broward, close to 18,000 new units heading to market. In Dubai, about three out of four homes sold in the first half of this year were off-plan. People bought from a drawing.

## Who creates the believers

In my experience, three players create them:

1. **The visionary.** The developer who sees a tower where everyone else sees a parking lot.
2. **The brand.** A hotel group, a fashion house or a car maker that puts its name next to the developer.
3. **The deep pockets.** The investors who commit before anyone else.

When these three hold hands, a city grows.

## The line is the product

Picture a nightclub with a long line outside. You cannot hear the music. You do not know who is inside. But the line is long, so you join it, because if so many people are waiting, it must be good. That is FOMO, the fear of missing out. And here is the secret: the line is the product.

Now imagine the line is shorter one night, and shorter again the next. Then people start walking out. Nobody wants to be the last one on the dance floor when the lights come on.

## What happened in Toronto

For years, the Toronto line was made mostly of investors. A study by Urbanation and CIBC found that investors were 70% or more of presale buyers. They did not plan to live in the building. They wanted the building to go up in value.

Then interest rates rose, and rents stopped covering mortgages. The same study found that about 70% of investors with a mortgage on a new condo were losing money every month. The line went home. Last year, new condo sales in the region fell to the lowest level since 1991. This year, investment groups are buying finished, unsold units for about 40% less than the original price in the same buildings.

## When the believers leave, the cranes leave

Part of you may smile at the investor who bought ten units on borrowed money and now pays every month for empty units. I understand that feeling. But here is the twist: when the believers leave, the cranes leave with them. The number of condos under construction around Toronto is now at its lowest level since early 2012, and analysts warn this sets the market up for a serious shortage by the end of the decade.

## Five signs a storm is coming

1. **The line is made of investors**, not people who want to live there.
2. **New costs much more than finished next door.** In Toronto today, an unsold new condo costs about 60% more per square foot than a resale.
3. **Rent no longer pays the mortgage.**
4. **Developers soften the deal** with incentives instead of cutting the price.
5. **Buyers start choosing finished homes** over presale. In Dubai, the share of ready homes sold rose from 24% to 29% in the third quarter of 2026.

## Is this a crash forecast?

No. To be fair, the 2026 UBS Global Real Estate Bubble Index placed both Miami and Dubai in the elevated risk category, not the highest one, and Miami actually cooled down from the top of the list. The storm is not here, at least not yet. But if you know where to look, you can see clouds on the horizon.

My opinion, and not financial or legal advice: do not just watch the cranes. Watch the believers. Rules change by country, so always check with a local lawyer.
takeaways: Off-plan markets run on belief that a unit will be worth more later.
Toronto new condo sales fell from almost 31,000 in 2021 to 60 in three months of summer 2026.
When investors make up most of the line, the market is fragile.
When believers leave, construction stops too, which can lead to future shortages.
Watch five signs: an investor-heavy line, a big new-versus-resale gap, rent below mortgage, softer deals and buyers turning to finished homes.
faq: Why did Toronto presale condo sales collapse?
Investors made up 70% or more of presale buyers. When interest rates rose and rents stopped covering mortgages, most of them stopped buying, and sales fell to the lowest level since 1991.
What are the warning signs of an off-plan market downturn?

An investor-heavy buyer base, new units priced far above nearby resales, rents that do not cover the mortgage, developers adding incentives instead of cutting prices, and buyers shifting to finished homes.
Are Miami and Dubai in a real estate bubble?
As reported in 2026, the UBS Global Real Estate Bubble Index placed both in the elevated risk category, not the highest one, and Miami cooled down from the top of the list.
What happens when presale buyers disappear?
New projects stop launching and construction slows. In Toronto, condos under construction reached the lowest level since early 2012, which analysts say could lead to a shortage.
